messages:
Maya: quick follow-up from this morning's RFC review — we need a concrete, low-risk first slice for the cross-cutting API stitch plan. thoughts?
Joel: +1 on small slice. prefer something that gives measurable cost win early. maybe the per-tenant routing table + adapter fabric instead of touching hotpath core.
Nina: agree — if we extract an adapter fabric that only handles enrichment adapters (not hotpath inference), we can iterate without touching kv cache or runtime. low blast radius.
Sam: can we get a perf checkout before/after? curious about overhead of the fabric (additional hop). want safe SLOs.
Maya: plan suggestion: 1) extract adapter-fabric service exposing lightweight gRPC facade 2) route enrichment traffic (non-kv, non-streaming) to the fabric 3) measure 90th perc latency and CPU cost delta for 2 weeks 4) decide next slice. keeps hotpath untouched.
Joel: sounds good. that lets us reduce code churn in runtime. can we do tenant cohorts: start with internal/alpha tenants then opt into beta?
Nina: yes — cohort rollout via feature flagging and route-override. also need a checklist: schema compatibility tests, contract fuzz, golden prompt regression run.
Sam: + checklist: add synthetic load that mirrors short bursts and long tails. include sampling for token-level traces (privacy-safe).
ArchBot: deploy-story created: infra/deploys/3570001234-fabric-slice (CI job, canary, metrics pipeline).
Maya: tradeoffs: increases surface area (another service to operate) vs. decreases coupling and makes future adapter refactors cheaper. goal is paydown velocity > ops cost within 3 sprints.
Joel: risk mitigation: keep fallback path to current enrichment path. if fabric latency spikes, route back automatically. add circuit-breaker with 10s SLA threshold.
Nina: contract plan: minimal protobufs (Request { tenant_id, payload_meta, payload_bytes } Response { status, payload_bytes }) — no semantic parsing in fabric. keeps it dumb and easy to replace.
Sam: ops ask: dashboards: per-route p50/p90/p99 latency, CPU, error rate, and cost-per-1k-requests. also tracer tags: fabric=true, cohort=alpha|beta. make alert for >3% error uplift vs baseline.
Maya: ownership: Nina will lead the adapter-fabric epic, Joel owns rollout plan, Sam owns infra and perf harness. I'll coordinate product sign-off and estimate.
Joel: timeline proposal: spike + test harness (1 sprint), implement fabric + adapter shims (1 sprint), alpha rollout + 2-week bake (1 sprint). total 3 sprints to first payoff.
Nina: noted. will start spike tomorrow. I'll post PRs for the proto and a lightweight shim library.
Sam: I'll scaffold the perf harness and add the canary alert playbook.
Maya: decision for the thread: proceed with the adapter-fabric first-slice as described, cohort rollout, keep hotpath untouched, instrument aggressively. action owners assigned.
Joel: :thumbsup:
Nina: :+1:
Sam: logging a follow-up: postmortem playbook if rollback needed — include quick DNS/route revert steps.
Maya: thanks all — will update the RFC doc with this plan and owners. we can iterate on scope after the spike.
